title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): this is the deformation theory of ordinary abelian varieties via p-divisible groups, as in the May 1966 letter to Tate. Over an Artin local base A with residue field of characteristic p, an ordinary p-divisible group is an extension of an étale part M by a multiplicative part N. Deformations of such an extension, trivialised over S_0, are classified by Ext^1(M,N). This Ext group is represented by a formal group: in effect the formal torus T_p(M)^∨ ⊗ N̂. These are the Serre–Tate canonical coordinates.

Given homomorphisms u: M→M' and v: N→N', a pair of extensions (ξ,ξ') admits a morphism E→E' compatible with u and v exactly when v_*(ξ) = u^*(ξ'). Hence such compatible pairs are represented by the kernel K of α−β : G×G' → H. Here G = T_p(M)^∨⊗N, G' = T_p(M')^∨⊗N', H = T_p(M)^∨⊗N', α is induced by v and β by u.

This page draws the consequence. In the situation of formal moduli with N, N' of multiplicative type ('de t.m.'), the formal variety of moduli of such systems is a formal group of multiplicative type over A. It is defined as the kernel of α−β, a homomorphism of formal groups of multiplicative type.

This applies in particular to the formal moduli of a polarised ordinary abelian variety. Take u, v to be the maps induced by the polarisation λ: X→X^t on the étale and toric parts. The polarised deformation space is then the kernel of a homomorphism of formal tori, i.e. a formal group of multiplicative type.

When A is the spectrum of a field of characteristic p>0, he deduces that the local moduli ring is a complete intersection (hence Cohen–Macaulay, 'C.M.'). It is not necessarily smooth: when deg λ is divisible by p, the kernel can be non-reduced, a multiplicative-type finite part times a torus. The next page states the conclusions:
- With polarisation and level ('Jacobi') rigidification, the moduli scheme in characteristic p is a local complete intersection at ordinary points.
- It is locally irreducible, and M_red is smooth.
- Comparison with characteristic 0 gives dimension g(g+1)/2 at every ordinary point.
- If the polarisation degree is prime to p, the moduli scheme is smooth there.
- A margin note flags the dimension count in the case where the degree is divisible by p.
errors: The transcription's 'α ≠ β' is almost certainly the condition α = β, i.e. the kernel of α−β. As written it is not a mathematical error by Grothendieck.

'Grauerstein' is unreadable as a name. It may refer to some standard commutative-algebra or analytic result used for the complete-intersection/CM conclusion; the argument itself is not checkable from the page.

The claim of local irreducibility with M_red smooth holds at ordinary points, since a multiplicative-type formal group has smooth reduced part. Grothendieck explicitly restricts to ordinary abelian varieties on the next page, so there is no gap there.

ideas.what: Deformations of an extension of an étale p-divisible group by a multiplicative one are represented by the formal torus T_p(M)^∨⊗N̂ (canonical coordinates).
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical coordinates / Serre–Tate local moduli
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate 1966 (circulated); related material in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and Montréal 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné'

ideas.what: Polarised (or morphism-compatible) deformations of ordinary p-divisible groups form the kernel of α−β between formal tori, hence a formal group of multiplicative type.
ideas.modern_name: Deformation space of a polarised ordinary abelian variety as a subtorus (symmetric part of the Serre–Tate torus); biextension viewpoint

ideas.what: Consequence: at ordinary points, moduli of polarised abelian varieties with level structure in char p is a local complete intersection, locally irreducible with smooth reduction, of dimension g(g+1)/2. It is smooth if the polarisation degree is prime to p.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of A_{g,d,n}⊗F_p at ordinary points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford/Oort for prime-to-p degree; Norman–Oort (1980) for dimension and lci of A_{g,d,n} in general

missed.claim: In 1966 Grothendieck already derived, via Serre–Tate coordinates and kernels of maps of formal tori, that polarised moduli at ordinary points (including degree divisible by p) are local complete intersections with smooth reduced part and dimension g(g+1)/2. This anticipates part of Norman–Oort (1980) restricted to the ordinary locus.
missed.quote: la variété formelle des modules ... est un groupe formel de t.m. sur A ... V.A. polarisée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority detail for the local structure of non-principally polarised moduli in char p. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the Serre–Tate/ordinary deformation theory familiar from the Tate letter, Messing, Mumford and Katz. The explicit 1966 treatment of non-prime-to-p polarisations (lci, M_red smooth) is a modest unpublished priority detail rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'α ≠ β' should read as the equaliser/kernel condition α = β (Ker(α−β)).
'V.A.' = variétés abéliennes; 'ordinaires' inserted above line 'V.A. polarisées'.
